theory.title: Exercise 3.2.5: Specific Exception Types
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "A timeout is not the same as bad data. A connection failure is not the same as a permission error. Different errors need different responses. That's why we can catch specific exception types."

Multiple EXCEPT Blocks

Use specific exception types to handle different errors differently:

TRY
    Risky Operation
EXCEPT    ValueError    AS    ${err}
    # Handle ValueError specifically
    Log    Bad value: ${err}
EXCEPT    TypeError    AS    ${err}
    # Handle TypeError specifically
    Log    Wrong type: ${err}
EXCEPT    AS    ${err}
    # Catch all other errors
    Log    Other error: ${err}
END

Common Error Types:

  • ValueError: Invalid value (e.g., int('abc'))
  • TypeError: Wrong data type
  • AssertionError: Failed assertion
  • * (or no type): Catches all errors

Example: Retry Logic for Timeouts

${attempts}=    Set Variable    0
WHILE    ${attempts} < 3
    TRY
        Log    Attempt ${attempts + 1}: Connecting...
        Fail    Connection timeout  # Simulates timeout
    EXCEPT    *timeout*    AS    ${err}
        Log    Timeout detected, retrying...
        ${attempts}=    Set Variable    ${attempts + 1}
    EXCEPT    AS    ${err}
        Log    Non-timeout error, aborting: ${err}
        BREAK
    END
END

Result: Retries on timeout, aborts on other errors.

⚠️ Multiple EXCEPT Tips

  • More specific EXCEPT blocks should come first
  • General EXCEPT (without type) catches all remaining errors
  • Can use glob patterns: EXCEPT *timeout*
  • EXCEPT without type acts as catch-all
  • Only ONE EXCEPT block executes (first match)
  • Use for retry logic, fallback values, error-specific logging
